scope: Pointer behavior of the visually rendered review dots on page264 only.

known_evidence.source_ax: Source exposes three real review tabs plus previous/next controls, but no numbered dot controls in the accessibility tree.
known_evidence.source_markup_style_evidence: Recovered source review CSS/markup evidence describes visual review dots as spans rather than button elements. Span markup alone does not prove pointer-inert behavior because JavaScript listeners could still be attached.
known_evidence.target_owner: Code Snippets ID14 AF reusable reviews controls v005 creates three .af-review-source-dot button controls and each pointer click activates/focuses the corresponding real Atomic tab.
known_evidence.page264_current_containment: Code Snippets ID33 sets tabindex=-1 and aria-hidden=true on the ID14 dot buttons after insertion. Visual appearance and ID14 pointer click behavior are intentionally preserved in the accepted semantic containment state.
known_evidence.global_plan: build/reviews-controls-v006-dot-a11y-plan.json proposed only the same tabindex/aria-hidden semantic change globally and explicitly preserved pointer click; it did not prove pointer parity with the source.

why_open: For exact behavior parity, source visual-dot pointer behavior must be observed directly. AX absence proves only keyboard/accessibility-tree parity, not whether a source span reacts to pointer clicks.
live_test_preconditions: Use exactly one synchronized source and one page264 target tab in an interaction-capable browser.
Verify the three source real tabs and target real Atomic tabs have the accepted exact names before testing dots.
Start source and target on the same real review/tab and record the selected tab/panel.
Do not modify ID14 or ID33 before this observation.
tests: Identify the three visible source review-dot hit areas and record their actual rendered element tags/classes plus cursor/pointer-events; do not infer behavior from AX absence.
Pointer-click source visual dot 2 while review 1 is selected and record whether the visible/selected review changes to 2.
Repeat source visual dot 3 and then dot 1; record whether focus changes, whether selection changes, and whether any URL/hash changes.
Run the identical pointer sequence on target .af-review-source-dot controls and record real Atomic tab/panel selection plus focus.
Repeat once after using previous/next to prove dot behavior is not a one-time initialization artifact.

decision_tree.source_dots_pointer_active_and_target_ma: PASS; preserve ID14 pointer behavior plus ID33 AX/focus containment. No write.
decision_tree.source_dots_pointer_inert_target_dots_ac: REAL_BEHAVIOR_DELTA. Before any code, read current ID14/ID33 and determine the smallest page264-only containment that prevents dot activation without changing dot visuals, previous/next, real tab keyboard behavior or global pages.
decision_tree.target_dots_missing_or_owner_changed: STOP and reconcile current runtime ownership before using this plan.

future_fix_constraints_if_mismatch_prove: Do not modify shared/global ID14 from page264 scope.
Prefer extending the existing page264 ID33 owner rather than creating a new snippet.
Preserve the three real Atomic tabs, previous/next controls, Arrow/Home/End handling and exact accessible names.
Preserve dot visual rendering if the source has decorative dots; only the proven extra pointer behavior may be contained.
No DOM rebuild or CSS pointer-events shortcut until focus/hover/visual consequences are measured.
